proposal.title: Droquasef: a translation workflow for free software
proposal.summary: Droquasef builds a translation workflow for free software for translators and their communities.

sections.heading: Problem
sections.text: Free software stays untranslated because translation tooling is fragmented. Translators and their communities depend on localisation every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

sections.heading: Approach
sections.text: We will build a translation workflow for free software called Droquasef. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

sections.heading: Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
sections.text: Localisation is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

sections.heading: Team and experience
sections.text: We maintain http://forge.test/droquasef/droquasef, which 392 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on localisation for 4 years.

sections.heading: Deliverables and licence
sections.text: All code will be released under the Apache-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/droquasef/droquasef. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

sections.heading: Milestones
sections.text: The work runs over 11 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8. Documentation and release ends in month 11.

sections.heading: Budget justification
sections.text: The plan asks for 53000.00 EUR for 79 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 600.00 EUR to 750.00 EUR.

proposal.narrative:
Problem
Free software stays untranslated because translation tooling is fragmented. Translators and their communities depend on localisation every day, yet the tools they have are hard to audit and slow to update.

Approach
We will build a translation workflow for free software called Droquasef. The work starts from a written threat model and ends with a reproducible release. Each component gets tests and a fuzz target before it is merged.

Relevance to the Open Internet Stack
Localisation is part of the Open Internet Stack. An open implementation lets anyone inspect, reuse and improve it without asking a vendor for permission.

Team and experience
We maintain http://forge.test/droquasef/droquasef, which 392 public projects depend on. Our team has worked on localisation for 4 years.

Deliverables and licence
All code will be released under the Apache-2.0 licence in http://forge.test/droquasef/droquasef. Documentation will be published under CC BY 4.0.

Milestones
The work runs over 11 months in 4 milestones. Design and threat model ends in month 2. Core implementation ends in month 5. Testing and fuzzing ends in month 8. Documentation and release ends in month 11.

Budget justification
The plan asks for 53000.00 EUR for 79 days of work over 4 tasks. Day rates range from 600.00 EUR to 750.00 EUR.
